advances: Proves a positive absolute lower bound for the original optimized logarithmic integral hitting score on every coordinate-unconditional four-point-width table, with arbitrary correlations among its folded coordinates. The proof includes the two-family down-set disjoint-pair inequality, convex extendability with zero entries, and an explicit constant requiring no numerical certificate. In fact the fixed center at a vertex of the inner Boolean cube suffices.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The source archive motivated the claim but is not used as a premise; the down-set inequality and all analytic estimates used here are proved above.
proof:
First verify the admissible class. Since \(h\) is decreasing and nonzero, \(h(\varnothing)>0\), \(w_{\max}=h(\varnothing)\), and \(\{0,1\}^n\subseteq D\). The family \(\mathcal F=\{S:h(S)>0\}\) is a down-set. Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}D\). If \(\mathbf y\in P\cap\mathbb Z^n\), then \(\mathbf y\in\{-1,0,1,2\}^n\). In any convex representation \(\mathbf y=\sum_j\lambda_j\mathbf z_j\) with \(\mathbf z_j\in D\) and \(\lambda_j>0\), each coordinate of \(\mathbf y\) equal to \(-1\) or \(2\) forces that same extreme coordinate in every \(\mathbf z_j\). Thus \(O(\mathbf y)\subseteq O(\mathbf z_j)\) for each \(j\). Down-closure implies \(O(\mathbf y)\in\mathcal F\), so \(\mathbf y\in D\). Therefore \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n=D\).

For the same reason, when \(\mathbf y\in D\) is any convex combination of points \(\mathbf z_j\in D\), monotonicity gives \(w_{\mathbf y}\ge w_{\mathbf z_j}\) for every active \(j\), and hence \(\phi_{\mathbf y}\le\phi_{\mathbf z_j}\). In particular \(\phi_{\mathbf y}\le\sum_j\lambda_j\phi_{\mathbf z_j}\). These are exactly the lattice-convexity and convex-admissibility hypotheses of the converse extension assertion in `488f0a583886b5fc`. More explicitly, on \(P\) form its finite convex roof

\[
\widehat\phi(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf z}\phi_{\mathbf z}:
\lambda_{\mathbf z}\ge0,\quad\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf z}=1,\quad
\sum_{\mathbf z\in D}\lambda_{\mathbf z}\mathbf z=x\right\}.
\]

The feasible coefficient set is nonempty and compact, so the minimum exists; combining feasible coefficient vectors proves convexity. Convex admissibility and the one-point representation give \(\widehat\phi(\mathbf y)=\phi_{\mathbf y}\) on \(D\). The function equal to \(h(\varnothing)e^{-\widehat\phi(x)}\) on \(P\) and zero outside \(P\) is finite-valued and log-concave. Indeed convexity proves log-concavity when both endpoints belong to \(P\), while otherwise the required right side is zero. Lattice convexity proves that this extension realizes every zero entry too.

Conversely, the coordinate reflections act transitively on the box points with a given outer-coordinate set, so an invariant table determines a function \(h\). Fix \(S\subseteq[n]\) and \(i\notin S\), holding all other coordinates at box values with outer-coordinate set \(S\). The values along coordinate \(i\) at \(-1,0,1,2\) are \(h(S\cup\{i\}),h(S),h(S),h(S\cup\{i\})\). If the endpoint value is positive, log-concavity of the extension at the interior points implies \(h(S)\ge h(S\cup\{i\})\); if it is zero the inequality follows from nonnegativity. Iteration gives all required inclusion inequalities, including zero entries.

We next prove the disjoint-pair engine. For down-sets \(\mathcal U,\mathcal V\subseteq2^{[r]}\), write

\[
\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)
=\#\{(A,C)\in\mathcal U\times\mathcal V:A\cap C=\varnothing\}.
\]

We claim that, with \(g=\kappa/2=\log(3)/\log(4)\in(0,1)\),
\(\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)\ge(|\mathcal U||\mathcal V|)^g\).
If either family is empty this is immediate. For \(r=0\), each nonempty family consists of the empty set and the claim is equality. Induct on \(r\). Split each family according to whether it contains coordinate \(r\), then delete that coordinate: \(\mathcal U_1\subseteq\mathcal U_0\) and \(\mathcal V_1\subseteq\mathcal V_0\) are down-sets on \([r-1]\). For nonempty original families, let \(x=|\mathcal U_0|>0\), \(y=|\mathcal V_0|>0\), \(u=|\mathcal U_1|/x\), and \(v=|\mathcal V_1|/y\), so \(u,v\in[0,1]\). The three possible disjoint coordinate states and induction give

\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)
&=\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U_0,\mathcal V_0)
+\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U_1,\mathcal V_0)
+\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U_0,\mathcal V_1)\\
&\ge(xy)^g(1+u^g+v^g).
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to show \(1+u^g+v^g\ge((1+u)(1+v))^g\). Let the left side minus the right side be \(f(u,v)\). For fixed \(u\) and \(0<v<1\), the sign of \(\partial_v f\) is the sign of
\(((1+v)/v)^{1-g}-(1+u)^g\), a strictly decreasing expression in \(v\). Consequently the derivative is either of one sign or changes from positive to negative, so continuity on \([0,1]\) implies that its minimum is at an endpoint. At \(v=0\), \(f(u,0)=1+u^g-(1+u)^g\ge0\): this function is zero at \(u=0\) and has nonnegative derivative for \(u>0\), since \(g-1<0\). At \(v=1\), the function is \(q(u)=2+u^g-2^g(1+u)^g\). On \(0<u<1\), its derivative has the sign of \(((1+u)/u)^{1-g}-2^g\), again strictly decreasing, so its minimum also occurs at an endpoint. These endpoints are \(q(0)=2-2^g>0\) and \(q(1)=3-4^g=0\). This proves the needed inequality at all boundary points as well, and completes induction. In particular,
\(\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal U,\mathcal U)\ge|\mathcal U|^\kappa\).

Return to the table. Put \(H=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}h(S)>0\). For each \(S\), exactly \(2^n\) box points have outer-coordinate set \(S\), so \(W=2^nH\). Dividing all weights by \(H\) leaves \(\phi\), the families of admissible supports, and all gaps unchanged, while dividing every hitting mass and score by \(H\). Thus it suffices to prove the fixed-center bound when \(\sum_Sh(S)=1\), which we now assume. Write \(h_0=h(\varnothing)>0\), and, only for \(S\in\mathcal F\), write \(\Phi(S)=\log(h_0/h(S))\). For \(t\ge0\), define the nonempty down-set \(\mathcal F_t=\{S\in\mathcal F:\Phi(S)\le t\}\), and put \(N(t)=|\mathcal F_t|\) and \(d(t)=\operatorname{DP}(\mathcal F_t,\mathcal F_t)\). These finite step functions satisfy \(1\le N(t)\le2^n\) and \(d(t)\ge N(t)^\kappa\). A finite-sum integration gives

\[
Z:=\int_0^\infty N(t)e^{-t}\,dt
=\sum_{S\in\mathcal F}e^{-\Phi(S)}
=\frac1{h_0}.
\]

We establish a lower bound for \(m_{\log}(\mathbf0,t;w)\) by disjoint reflection pairs. A vector \(\mathbf y\) for which both \(\mathbf y\) and \(-\mathbf y\) belong to the box has coordinates in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). The map
\(\mathbf y\mapsto(A,C)\), where \(A=\{i:y_i=-1\}\) and \(C=\{i:y_i=1\}\), is a bijection with ordered disjoint set pairs. Its two weights are \(h(A)\) and \(h(C)\), and its two potentials are \(\Phi(A)\) and \(\Phi(C)\) whenever both are positive. If \(A,C\in\mathcal F_t\), then both potentials are at most \(t\).

For \(\mathbf y\ne\mathbf0\), the pair \(\{\mathbf y,-\mathbf y\}\) is an affinely independent support with barycenter \(\mathbf0\), equal barycentric coefficients, and gap \((\phi_{\mathbf y}+\phi_{-\mathbf y})/2\le t\), since \(\phi_{\mathbf0}=0\). Every hitting set therefore contains at least one endpoint. Distinct unordered reflection pairs are disjoint and avoid the compulsory singleton \(\{\mathbf0\}\). Equivalently, in the exact closed-cap formula (15) of `488f0a583886b5fc`, for a normal \((\mathbf b,s)\ne(\mathbf0,0)\) with \(s\ge0\), the two cap expressions sum to \(s(2t-\phi_{\mathbf y}-\phi_{-\mathbf y})\ge0\); at least one is nonnegative. This also covers \(s=0\), all equality atoms, and the central point. Hence, defining the ordered sum

\[
\Sigma(t)=\sum_{\substack{A,C\in\mathcal F_t\\A\cap C=\varnothing}}
\min(h(A),h(C)),
\]

we have \(m_{\log}(\mathbf0,t;w)\ge(h_0+\Sigma(t))/2\). The correction \(h_0\) makes the single ordered pair \((\varnothing,\varnothing)\) contribute its full central mass; every other ordered pair is matched with its distinct reversal.

For an ordered pair in \(\mathcal F_t\), put \(r=\max(\Phi(A),\Phi(C))\in[0,t]\). The elementary identity \(e^{-r}=e^{-t}+\int_r^te^{-\tau}\,d\tau\), summed over the finitely many such pairs, yields the exact layer-cake formula

\[
\Sigma(t)=h_0\left(e^{-t}d(t)+\int_0^t d(\tau)e^{-\tau}\,d\tau\right).
\]

The endpoint term retains pairs entering exactly at \(t\), so ties and \(t=0\) cause no exception. Define \(\Psi(t)=\int_0^t N(\tau)^\kappa e^{-\tau}\,d\tau\). Discarding only nonnegative terms and using the disjoint-pair inequality gives
\(m_{\log}(\mathbf0,t;w)\ge\Psi(t)/(2Z)\).

Let \(q=\sup_{t\ge0}m_{\log}(\mathbf0,t;w)/(1+t)\). It is finite because \(m_{\log}\le W=2^n\), and positive because every admissible hitting set contains \(\mathbf0\). More precisely,
\(q\ge h_0=1/Z\) and \(\Psi(t)\le2qZ(1+t)\) for all \(t\ge0\).

Fix \(0<a<1/\kappa'\). The function \(\Psi\) is absolutely continuous, with \(\Psi(0)=0\), derivative \(N(t)^\kappa e^{-t}\) almost everywhere, and \(0\le\Psi(t)\le2^{n\kappa}\). Thus integration by parts on \([0,R]\), followed by \(R\to\infty\), has zero boundary terms at both endpoints and gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^\infty N(t)^\kappa e^{-t}e^{-a\kappa t}\,dt
&=a\kappa\int_0^\infty\Psi(t)e^{-a\kappa t}\,dt\\
&\le2qZ\,a\kappa\int_0^\infty(1+t)e^{-a\kappa t}\,dt\\
&=2qZ\left(1+\frac1{a\kappa}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

All integrals are finite: \(N\) and \(\Psi\) are bounded, \(a>0\), and the displayed exponential rates are positive. Apply Hölder with conjugate exponents \(\kappa,\kappa'>1\) to \(N(t)e^{-at}\) and \(e^{at}\) on the measure space \(([0,\infty),e^{-t}dt)\). The second factor is integrable to power \(\kappa'\) precisely because \(a\kappa'<1\). Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
Z
&\le\left(\int_0^\infty N(t)^\kappa e^{-t}e^{-a\kappa t}\,dt\right)^{1/\kappa}
\left(\int_0^\infty e^{a\kappa't}e^{-t}\,dt\right)^{1/\kappa'}\\
&\le(2qZ)^{1/\kappa}
\left(1+\frac1{a\kappa}\right)^{1/\kappa}
(1-a\kappa')^{-1/\kappa'}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(Z\ge1/q\), dividing by \(Z^{1/\kappa}\) and then using this lower bound gives

\[
q^{-1/\kappa'}\le Z^{1/\kappa'}
\le(2q)^{1/\kappa}
\left(1+\frac1{a\kappa}\right)^{1/\kappa}
(1-a\kappa')^{-1/\kappa'}.
\]

As \(1/\kappa+1/\kappa'=1\), this is exactly \(q\ge c(a)\). For \(a=1/5\), admissibility follows without approximation: \(\kappa>3/2\) because \(3^2>2^3\), so \(1<\kappa'<3\) and \(\kappa'/5<1\). Every factor of the asserted \(c_{\mathrm Q}\) is therefore a finite positive real number.

The supremum defining \(q\) is attained. Indeed the finite family \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf0}\) changes its cutoff membership only at finitely many values \(G_E\), all in \([0,B]\). The hitting mass is constant between successive such values, including the value at the left endpoint, while division by \(1+t\) decreases there. Beyond \(B\) every support is included and the ratio again decreases. Consequently one of those finitely many cutoffs, including zero, attains the maximum. This also handles \(B=0\). Equation (15) of `488f0a583886b5fc` now gives the stated all-cap assertion at this fixed cutoff. Undoing normalization multiplies \(q\) by \(H=2^{-n}W\), proving the theorem.

The coordinate reflections preserve weights and all barycentric gaps and carry \(\mathbf0\) to any chosen vertex of \(\{0,1\}^n\), which proves the other-center assertion. A unimodular affine map \(\mathbf y\mapsto U\mathbf y+\mathbf v\), with \(U\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)\) and \(\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^n\), bijects lattice points and barycentric supports, preserves their coefficients and potentials, and hence preserves every hitting mass, total mass, and optimized score. Composing the log-concave extension with the inverse affine map also preserves global extendability. This proves the asserted affine invariance. Throughout, finite positive support alone was used after down-set monotonicity; weights of different sets were never factorized. If one additionally allows \(h\equiv0\), its global extension is the zero function and its mass inequality is trivial with score defined as zero; it is outside the nonzero-table convention of the accepted predecessor.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\), and let \(h:2^{[n]}\to[0,\infty)\) be nonzero and decreasing under inclusion. On \(\mathbb Z^n\), define

\[
w_{\mathbf y}=\begin{cases}
h(O(\mathbf y)),&\mathbf y\in\{-1,0,1,2\}^n,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad O(\mathbf y)=\{i:y_i\in\{-1,2\}\}.
\]

This is a globally extendable finite table in the exact sense of accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`: a finite-valued nonnegative log-concave function on \(\mathbb R^n\) agrees with the table at every lattice point, including its zeros. Conversely, every nonzero globally extendable table supported in \(\{-1,0,1,2\}^n\) and invariant under each coordinate reflection \(y_i\mapsto1-y_i\) has this form.

Use the canonical notation of `488f0a583886b5fc`: \(D=\{\mathbf y:w_{\mathbf y}>0\}\), \(W=\sum_Dw_{\mathbf y}\), \(w_{\max}=\max_Dw_{\mathbf y}\), \(\phi_{\mathbf y}=\log(w_{\max}/w_{\mathbf y})\), and \(B=\max_D\phi_{\mathbf y}\). For \(\mathbf J\in D\), let \(\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\) consist of the nonempty affinely independent sets \(E\subseteq D\) having \(\mathbf J\) in their relative-interior convex hull, with positive barycentric coefficients \(\lambda_{E,\mathbf y}\). Put \(G_E=\sum_{\mathbf y\in E}\lambda_{E,\mathbf y}\phi_{\mathbf y}-\phi_{\mathbf J}\). For \(L\ge0\), define

\[
\begin{aligned}
m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)
&=\min\left\{\sum_{\mathbf y\in F}w_{\mathbf y}:F\subseteq D,\
F\cap E\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }E\in\mathcal E_{\mathbf J}\text{ with }G_E\le L\right\},\\
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)
&=\max_{\mathbf J\in D,\,L\ge0}\frac{m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)}{1+L}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the source's \(\mathcal B(w)\) is exactly \(\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\); it is not the canonical amplitude \(B\).

Set \(\kappa=\log(3)/\log(2)\) and \(\kappa'=\kappa/(\kappa-1)\). For every \(a\) with \(0<a<1/\kappa'\), set

\[
c(a)=2^{-1/\kappa}
\left(1+\frac{1}{a\kappa}\right)^{-1/\kappa}
(1-a\kappa')^{1/\kappa'}.
\]

Then

\[
\max_{L\ge0}\frac{m_{\log}(\mathbf0,L;w)}{1+L}
\ \ge\ c(a)\,2^{-n}W,
\qquad
\mathcal B_{\log}^{\mathrm{hit}}(w)\ \ge\ c(a)\,2^{-n}W.
\]

In particular, the following exact absolute coefficient is valid:

\[
c_{\mathrm Q}=2^{-1/\kappa}
\left(1+\frac5\kappa\right)^{-1/\kappa}
\left(1-\frac{\kappa'}5\right)^{1/\kappa'}>0.
\]

Equivalently, some \(L\ge0\), fixed before choosing a slope, makes every closed lifted cap through \((\mathbf0,L)\) have table mass at least \(c_{\mathrm Q}(1+L)2^{-n}W\), including vertical lifted caps in equation (15) of `488f0a583886b5fc`. In particular this holds for every ordinary slope cap \(\{\mathbf y\in D:\phi_{\mathbf y}\le L+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf y\}\). By reflection symmetry any vertex of \(\{0,1\}^n\) can replace \(\mathbf0\). The score bound is also invariant under unimodular affine changes of lattice coordinates. No product representation of \(h\) is assumed.
